questions.question: When you see a green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, watch for pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection. You may drive through, but be ready to slow down or stop if the light changes.

questions.question: When you are in a travel lane on the road:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may back up if you take the wrong freeway entrance.
Don't stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you find a safe place to pull off. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Do something to get back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and get away from an aggressive driver. Trying to get revenge can make the situation worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off fog and make it harder to see. You can also use fog lights if your car has them.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and get ready to stop.
Must stop and check for traffic before going.
May drive through if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can drive through if the road is clear. You can also turn left or right unless a sign says you can't. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a car on your right. You should:

options.text: Slow down and let them go first.
Drive through and make them stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let them go first.
questions.explanation: The car on your right has the right-of-way. Slow down and let them pass first, then you may go.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop at a railroad crossing. If lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never go around the gate.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you should:

options.text: Let drivers on the public road go first.
Assume other drivers will move for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let drivers on the public road go first.
questions.explanation: Let drivers on the public road pass first. Merge safely when you have room.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Don't look at them, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't look at them, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between you and the aggressive driver. Slow down and let them go. Don't make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: When roads are wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, near pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the road conditions
Staying too close to other vehicles

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and result in a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair driving. This includes alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines (both prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear before moving.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before you move right or left.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get away from it.
Stop immediately and block its path.
Do everything you can to clear the path for the emergency vehicle.
Signal the emergency vehicle when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear the path for the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must do everything you can to give an emergency vehicle a clear path. If it is safe, pull your vehicle to the side of the road.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis can result from:

options.text: Staring at the road for long periods.
Getting too much sleep before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for long periods.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead without checking around your vehicle. This causes you to zone out and not notice traffic slowing or stopping ahead.

questions.question: The best way to prevent hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water and puddles.

questions.explanation: Wet roads make cars stop slowly and skid on turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must have your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle when driving. You must show all three documents if stopped.

questions.question: What helps someone overcome the effects of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will allow a person's body to get over the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must and must not do. This sign means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, parking, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you plan to do and helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes — another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a slow crash.
All passengers must use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Fasten your seat belt before you drive. Make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under must ride in a rear seat with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with an airbag.

questions.question: When is passing another vehicle not allowed?
questions.explanation: You cannot pass another vehicle on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These are unsafe and illegal passing zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is on top and green is on bottom. On a horizontal traffic signal, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread.
Slow down when driving in rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires with good tread and properly inflated. Slow down when driving in the rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, all drivers must stop. The driver who arrived first goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Do not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Spend a few minutes getting familiar with the vehicle's controls and equipment before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes getting familiar with the vehicle's controls and equipment before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to find and understand the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red lights and gates are active.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger signals you to stop, if there is a stop sign, or if flashing red lights and gates are active.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving?

options.text: It helps driving skills but damages judgment.
It damages both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on driving skills or judgment.
It damages judgment but not driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It damages both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts many driving skills. It slows your reaction time and affects your vision. It also damages your judgment of speed and distance. Alcohol lowers your inhibitions and makes you more likely to take risks.
